extracted.intended_audience: writers seeking agents/editors; agents & editors who list wants
extracted.subtask_description: Overview/homepage for Manuscript Wish List (MSWL), a platform where agents and editors state what they want to receive and where writers can find craft- and submission-focused resources (events, podcasts, blog posts) to tailor manuscripts and queries to agent preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match agent/editor wishlist
rubrics_metrics.description: What do you wish you had in your inbox?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core site mission: agents and editors declare what they'd like to receive so writers can target submissions. (Page presents MSWL as a searchable, human-curated database for querying agents' stated preferences.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing, Structure & Symmetry (make work addictive)
rubrics_metrics.description: How To Make Your Work More Addictive: Pacing, Structure & Symmetry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Event/topic emphasizing that addictive books rely on effective pacing, structural choices, and symmetry; implies manuscripts should pay attention to pacing, structural coherence, and balanced arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial potential
rubrics_metrics.description: How To Make Your Work More Commercial
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Event/topic focused on shaping manuscripts to be commercially appealing—consider marketability, hook, audience, and selling points when preparing work for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: The formula for successful books
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Session title implying there are recognizable patterns/structural elements that contribute to success; writers should study genre expectations, plot/character beats, and market trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of feedback — curation and application
rubrics_metrics.description: The Art of Feedback: What To Take, What To Ignore & How To Know The Difference
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance about interpreting editorial/peer feedback: discern which suggestions strengthen the work and which can be ignored; demonstrates that revision choices are evaluative criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character complexity and tension
rubrics_metrics.description: Messy Characters, Building Tension & How Agents Should Advocate For Your Work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the importance of nuanced (messy) characters and sustained tension; agents value characters who create stakes and advocate for projects with compelling conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres, tropes, trends, and agent fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Genres, Tropes, Trends, and Finding Your Agent Fit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should understand genre conventions, current trends and tropes and align their manuscript to agents who represent that space; agent fit is a selection criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Querying craft and persistence
rubrics_metrics.description: Querying, Middle School, And How Mistakes + Embarrassment Often Lead To Book Deals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights querying process as skillful and iterative; resilience and learning from mistakes are practical considerations in submission strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing for broad/international success
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing For Your International Bestseller: Liv Constantine on Crafting Unputdownable Characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Session implies criteria for international/bestseller potential: unputdownable characters and broadly resonant hooks; attention to wide appeal without losing specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author positioning and finding voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding Your Voice: On the Page, In Your Life
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice and author positioning are central selection criteria—distinctive voice and clear author positioning help manuscripts and authors stand out to agents/editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hook and pitch craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Hollywood Versus New York: Publishing, Film, Options, Etiquette + What Makes A Hook?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes consideration of what constitutes a strong hook; pitches should clearly communicate premise and marketable elements to attract industry attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional range, sensory detail, and handling difficult topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotional Range, Sensory Details, And Pitching Works On Difficult Topics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should demonstrate emotional depth and sensory specificity, and show awareness of how to responsibly pitch and handle sensitive subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metaphor, clarity, and editorial craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaphor, Math, Editing, & How You Can Get Your Message to Your Reader Effectively
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on use of figurative language, precision, and editing choices to communicate effectively; implicates clarity, restraint, and craft as evaluative factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events, podcasts, and educational resources as criteria signals
rubrics_metrics.description: MSWL provides events, podcasts, and blog posts on craft and submission topics (e.g., consultations, recorded panels, editor consultations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of curated educational content signals the site's role in translating agent/editor preferences into actionable craft and submission guidance; writers should use these resources to align work with industry expectations.
